source.title: SC-LoRA: Balancing Efficient Fine-tuning and Knowledge Preservation via Subspace-Constrained LoRA
source.authors: Min-Rui Luo; Fu-Hang Kuang; Yu Wang; Zi-Rui Liu; Tian-Xing He

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes an aligned chat model on benign and poisoned data and measures harmfulness, but its focus is comparing LoRA initializations for safety preservation rather than replicating the original fine-tuning study.
record.gate_note: Safety results from the study's own fine-tuning experiments are recorded. Cited findings from other work are not rows. The paper also reports downstream-task utility, which does not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Its baselines (full fine-tuning, vanilla LoRA, PiSSA, CorDA IPA) fine-tune Llama-2-7b-Chat on benign Samsum and on MetaMathQA with 256 harmful pairs mixed in. It scores harmfulness on Qi et al.'s 330 malicious questions. Measure and prompts follow the originals, but the judge is DeepSeek-V3 and the harmful data is a 1% poison, not harmful-only tuning. The paper's focus is its own SC-LoRA initialization.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that SC-LoRA balances downstream utility with preservation of safety and world knowledge, beating other LoRA initializations. They also report that ordinary fine-tuning baselines, except CorDA KPA, degrade safety, and that β controls the trade-off. Preservation can drop with longer or more complex fine-tuning, and with 64 or fewer initialization samples.
record.recipe_differences: Uses aligned-model fine-tuning and harmfulness evaluation, but focuses on comparing initialization methods; benign data is Samsum and harmful data is a 1% poison in MetaMathQA, rather than harmful-only fine-tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by fine-tuning method, SC-LoRA β setting, and SC-LoRA initialization sample count.

fits_no_version.finding: Subspace-constrained LoRA initialization (SC-LoRA β=0.9, and CorDA KPA) keeps harmfulness at base level under both benign and 1%-poisoned fine-tuning. Protection weakens at lower β and with fewer initialization samples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Constraining LoRA updates away from refusal-data activation subspaces at initialization prevents fine-tuning-induced safety loss.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
record.problems: One seed for all experiment results. The safety experiments use one model, one benign dataset, one poisoned-data setup, and a DeepSeek-V3 judge; no uncertainty estimates are reported. Poisoning tests 1% harmful pairs mixed into a larger dataset, not harmful-only fine-tuning.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported safety harmfulness results were left out. The initialization-sample results duplicated in Appendix E, Table 5 are recorded once from Section 4.5, Table 4.

untested.parts: Harmful-only fine-tuning, sweeps over harmful example counts, other models, and whether refusal is removed near-totally.
Benign datasets other than Samsum (e.g. Alpaca, Dolly, selected benign data), other models, multiple epochs.
Not tested. SC-LoRA constrains a subspace but does not measure where safety is localized.

missing.what: Learning-rate sweep of LoRA-based baselines (2e-5, 5e-5, 1e-4) on safety under poisoning; LoRA shows a sharp safety decline at higher lr. Table 3 reports only the best lr per baseline.
missing.locator: Section 4.3 text; Appendix C, Figure 6 (and Figure 5 for Samsum)

record.verdict_notes: The extractor misaligned Table 3 values. The CorDA KPA rows carry IPA's numbers, and the SC-LoRA β=0.5 rows carry KPA's; the correct β=0.5 values are HR 10.91%, HS 1.630. In Table 2, the β=0.5 and β=0.7 HS values are swapped. The record's V1 limits_scope label rested on SC-LoRA rows, which are the study's own mitigation method, so it was dropped. Base-model control rows are left as references. All results come from one seed with no uncertainty, one model, and a DeepSeek-V3 judge.

versions.untested_parts: The poisoned-data experiment uses 1% harmful pairs in a 25,600-sample dataset (256 harmful pairs), not harmful-only fine-tuning. It does not sweep harmful fine-tuning counts or establish near-total refusal removal.
Tests one benign dataset, Samsum, on Llama-2-7b-Chat; does not test other benign-data types or models.

relationships.condition: Llama-2-7b-Chat; full FT, vanilla LoRA, PiSSA, CorDA IPA; MetaMathQA with 256 harmful pairs (1%); 1 epoch; best learning rate
relationships.reason: HR rose from 1.212% to 23.94%, 23.64%, 29.39% and 67.27% (p-full-hr, p-lora-hr, p-pissa-hr, p-ipa-hr). Substantial, though short of near-total compliance.
relationships.display_finding: The harmful rate rose from 1.212% to 23.94% with full fine-tuning, 23.64% with LoRA, 29.39% with PiSSA and 67.27% with CorDA IPA. The rise is substantial but short of near-total compliance.

relationships.condition: Vanilla LoRA at learning rate 2e-5 under poisoning (text and Figure 6 only)
relationships.reason: Text says LoRA at lr=2e-5 preserves safety well, with a sharp decline only at higher lr, so the effect depends on learning rate. No row records this; text-based.
relationships.display_finding: LoRA at a learning rate of 2e-5 preserved safety well, with a sharp decline only at higher learning rates.

relationships.condition: Llama-2-7b-Chat; full FT, vanilla LoRA, PiSSA, CorDA IPA; Samsum, 1 epoch
relationships.reason: HR rose from 1.212% to 5.455%, 2.424%, 4.242% and 3.333% (b-full-hr, b-lora-hr, b-pissa-hr, b-ipa-hr). Small absolute rises, one seed, no uncertainty.
relationships.display_finding: The harmful rate rose from 1.212% to 5.455% (full), 2.424% (LoRA), 4.242% (PiSSA) and 3.333% (CorDA IPA), small rises from one seed with no reported uncertainty.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Full fine-tuning, vanilla LoRA, PiSSA and CorDA IPA on the 1%-poisoned MetaMathQA dataset
reader_labels.reason: Harmfulness rates rose from 1.212% to 23.94%, 23.64%, 29.39% and 67.27%, respectively; the measured effect is substantial but not reported as near-total refusal removal (p-full-hr, p-lora-hr, p-pissa-hr, p-ipa-hr).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SC-LoRA poisoned-data settings and the initialization-sample ablation
reader_labels.reason: SC-LoRA at β = 0.5 and β = 0.9 has no harmfulness-rate increase, while β = 0.7 and lower initialization-sample settings show smaller increases; this is not a uniform effect across methods or settings (p-sc05-hr, p-sc07-hr, p-sc09-hr, init-p256-hr, init-p128-hr, init-p64-hr, init-p32-hr).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Full fine-tuning, vanilla LoRA, PiSSA, CorDA IPA, and SC-LoRA at β = 0.5 or 0.7 on Samsum
reader_labels.reason: Their harmfulness rates exceed the pre-fine-tuning reference of 1.212% (b-full-hr, b-lora-hr, b-pissa-hr, b-ipa-hr, b-sc05-hr, b-sc07-hr).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CorDA KPA and SC-LoRA at β = 0.9 on Samsum
reader_labels.reason: These settings do not raise the harmfulness rate over the pre-fine-tuning reference (b-kpa-hr, b-sc09-hr).
